newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds see dollar issuance continue.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds see dollar issuance continue.

text.p: Dollar Eurobonds continued to surface on Wednesday, after a slew of sizeable issues in yesterday's trading session.
France Telecom launched its debut international financing, a $400 million five-year deal at 15 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes.
Dealers said the bond had gone quite slowly, although France Telecom was a high-rated credit.
"We have not sold any bonds yet," said a syndicate manager at a U.S. bank. "There is a bit of a cloud over French names at the moment."
Another dealer said the launch spread could have been one pip wider, but expected the issue to sell.
"Demand for five-year paper remains strong though, and this issue is large enough to get some institutional interest," the official at a European bank said.
At the retail end, Deutsche Bank launched a self-led $250 million December 1998 bond which an official there said was tapping into strong demand for short-dated dollar paper.
The launch spread was flat to U.S. Treasuries, which looked tight but compared well to outstanding paper which was trading below government bonds, dealers said.
"The level of demand has led to tighter spreads in the secondary markets," said a Deutsche Morgan Grenfell official.
"Comparable bonds are trading at six or seven b.p. below Treasuries, so this issue is also likely to tighten," he said.
Dealers said the dollar sector should take a breather now in order to absorb yesterday's flood of new deals.
Ten-year dollars in particular were looking a bit heavy, with sales of the EIB $1.0 billion issue, due to be priced later, a little sluggish.
Fannie Mae is due to price a $500 million 10-year bond, and TVA's 1.5 billion mark 10-year issue will also be priced later.
Elsewhere, plans for South Africa's upcoming mark Eurobond firmed up, with a seven-year maturity now considered likely.

"One of the objectives of our foreign debt strategy is to extend the maturity profile of our foreign debt. As a result we are looking at something in the seven-year region," the deputy director of South Africa's finance department Mario Ramos said.
Officials are visiting European financial centres this week ahead of an expected 500 million mark issue. Lead managers are Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and Morgan Stanley.
The delegation was in Amsterdam on Wednesday.
